hints: Notice the glider moves at constant speed, so resultant force is zero and $L + R + W = 0$ as vectors.
Notice the given directions: $W$ is vertically down, $R$ is $15^\circ$ above the horizontal to the right, and $L$ is tilted left of vertical.
Connect zero resultant to a closed head-to-tail triangle with $W$ longest and vertical and $R$ shortest, then look for $R$ pointing right and $L$ pointing up-left.
walkthrough: Constant speed in a straight line means equilibrium by Newton's first law, so the vector sum of $L$, $R$ and $W$ is zero.
From the glider diagram, $W$ acts vertically downwards, $R$ acts backwards along the flight path at $15^\circ$ above the horizontal to the right, and $L$ acts upwards tilted to the left of vertical.
For zero resultant the three force arrows placed head-to-tail must form a closed triangle, preserving each direction.
Therefore the triangle must have a long vertical-down side for $W$, a short side pointing right and slightly up for $R$, and a long side pointing up and slightly left for $L$.
Only the triangle with $W$ down on the left, $R$ small to the right at the bottom, and $L$ closing up the right side satisfies all three directions and the relative lengths. This is option D.

options.A: One side points to the left and downwards, whereas $R$ on the glider points to the right at $15^\circ$ above the horizontal, so the directions do not match.
options.B: The long vertical side is drawn acting upwards, whereas $W$ must act vertically downwards, so it cannot represent the weight in a head-to-tail triangle.
options.C: The short side representing $R$ points to the left, opposite to the air resistance direction up the $15^\circ$ slope to the right shown on the glider.
options.D: The long vertical-down side is $W$, the short side to the right is $R$ at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal, and the long tilted side is $L$ up and to the left, closing to zero resultant.
